newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry seen slowing in 2nd half-CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry seen slowing in 2nd half-CNI.

text.p: The strong growth in Brazilian industrial activity at the start of the second quarter of this year will not carry over into the second half, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
In April, industrial sales rose a record seasonally adjusted 13.12 percent on March, the highest ever monthly rise since the CNI began calculating the data in January 1992.

"These results should not be seen as a trend toward an overheating of the economy," The CNI said in a statement. "They were the result of a number of factors coming together at the same time, but which are unlikely to repeat themselves in the next few months."

The CNI said the stockpiling of goods which occurred in April in anticipation of credit restrictions coming into force now would bring about a decline in consumer demand in the last two months of the first half of 1997.

Statistics show that the monthly income of families has been rising at a slower rate since the beginning of the year and the level of indebtedness has also reached a level which leaves little room for consumers to take up further credit, the CNI said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
